# Species, models and potentials

Adds to `physics.instructions.md`, which applies as well.

- Species (`ball_impl::species`): a ball stores a `SpeciesId`; mass, `σ`, `ε`, colour and `display_radius` come from the world's `SpeciesTable`, one `Arc` owned by `BallPhysics` and shared with the `BallFactory` (`with_species`, `use_species`) and every `RendererSnapshot`. It is resolved once (`ResolvedSpecies`, from `WorldFile::validate` or `SimConfig::validated_species`). Never look species up in `SpeciesTable::builtin()` outside tests and the default. A config `[[species]]` list replaces the whole table; its first entry is the default. A new built-in species is converted from Å, K and u with `UnitSystem::REDUCED`; saves hold their own table (`save-format` skill). `display_radius` must not reach the physics.
- Models (#425): a species has one `Model` (`ball_impl::interaction`); inertia and sites derive from it (`Model::inertia`, `Species::sites`: 2D body-frame offsets, an atom is one site at the centre), never separate fields. Code outside `interaction` uses the sites (`SpeciesTable::sites`) and never matches on `Model`. A new model adds its `Model` variant, its arms in `Species::sites` and `pair_interactions`, its `SpeciesConfig` keys (`resolve`, `From<&Species>`: the only other place that matches on `Model`), and an `Interaction` variant if it brings a law.
- Interactions: what a model adds beyond the pair table is an `Interaction` variant (an enum, no trait objects: `cutoff`, `omega_sq`, `eval`), compiled per species pair by `pair_interactions`, only between equal parameters unless the law mixes them (pairs stay symmetric). The SIMD kernel hands each pair to the `each_pair` hook of `force_simd` only for species with interactions among those present, so atom runs stay bit-identical. A pair's cutoff is the largest of its potential and interactions; its time step limit includes their `omega_sq`. Every `eval` is the exact derivative of its energy (finite-difference tests).
- Time step limits are derived per species pair (`BallPhysics::time_step_limit`, `ω·dt ≤ 2π/20`); never hand-set them. Code that steps the world uses `MainContent::active_time_step`, not `time_step()`.
- Orientation (#348): a species with inertia has `θ`, `ω`, `α` on its balls (`Ball2D`, hot), drifted in the position update and kicked from `ForceResult::torque`. Every kinetic energy or temperature sum includes `½ I ω²` (`LocalKineticStats`: one degree of freedom per rotating ball); balls without inertia stay bit-identical (guard with `inertia > 0`).
- MB water (#349) and rigid molecules (#406): water's Lennard-Jones disk goes through the pair table, its hydrogen bonds are `Interaction::HBond` (water of equal parameters only). A molecule has `ε = 0` and an envelope `σ` (a null pair, `PairLaw::is_null`) and interacts through `SitePairs`. Config overrides naming a species with more than one site are rejected: they would not reach the sites.
- Pair potentials (`ball_impl::pair_potential`): a `PairLaw` is the bare law, `CappedPotential` adds the cap and the cutoff shift, a `PairTable` holds one per species pair (Lorentz–Berthelot, except `PairOverride`s, `BallPhysics::pair_overrides()`). `CapSettings` is fixed when the potential is built (`BallPhysics::cap_settings()`); `PhysicsConstants` holds only runtime settings. A new law implements `PairLaw` (scalar and `Lanes`), gets a `Potential` variant and an arm in `simd_forces::force_simd`, which dispatches once per ball; no per-neighbour branching in the kernel (`CappedLanes::gather`).
- External fields (`[[fields]]`, #347): implement `ExternalField` (`acceleration = −∇U / m`), get a `Field` variant, and act in the kick, on new balls (`add_ball_and_register`) and in a potential-energy pass in ball order; runs without fields stay bit-identical.
- Config rules (`sim_config/`): a rule about one key stays in its section's `resolve()`; a rule that involves several sections (overrides against the species table, molecule species) goes into `ResolvedSpecies::validate`, on the resolved config, and checks species by their properties, never by name. A new range or rule extends the generator of `tests/config_validation.rs`.
